claims.text: Ni-based superalloys with tuned interface coherency can serve as a model system for the transition from diffusion-dominated to dislocation-driven creep in HEA multilayers.
The proposed initial material is a Ni-based HEA multilayer with coherent interfaces.
The proposed initial material has a refined microstructure.
Changing composition or layer thickness can adjust interface coherency in a Ni-based HEA multilayer.
Both diffusion and dislocation motion are thermally activated at approximately 0.5–0.7 of the alloy melting temperature.
Highly coherent interfaces reduce dislocation activity at lower temperatures.
Reduced dislocation activity caused by highly coherent interfaces promotes diffusion-controlled creep.
Partial loss of interface coherency increases dislocation mobility.
Increased dislocation mobility following partial loss of coherency produces dislocation-controlled creep at higher temperatures.
Higher interface coherence or lower applied stress favors diffusion-mediated creep.
Partial interface incoherency or higher applied stress favors dislocation-mediated creep.
The creep-mechanism transition becomes less pronounced when the interface loses coherence.
The transition becomes less pronounced when stress and temperature are far outside the regimes in which diffusion or dislocation motion dominates.
Transition temperatures and stresses depend on alloy composition and microstructure.

contradictions.description: The mechanism and predicted outcome state that partial loss of coherency drives the transition toward dislocation-mediated creep, whereas the boundary states that loss of coherence makes the transition less pronounced. The distinction between initiating the transition and suppressing its observability is not explained.
